image_description: The image displays a collection of bicycle components, specifically focusing on disc brake rotors and calipers, resting on a wooden surface. There are two distinct rotor assemblies visible: one on the left with a silver, drilled rotor and a black caliper featuring red/white branding, and another on the right with a similar rotor and a caliper that has yellow accents. Black hydraulic hoses connect the calipers to the rest of the assembly. The components appear to be high-performance mountain bike parts.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both assemblies feature large, thin, circular metallic discs consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Black mechanical housings (calipers) are clearly positioned to straddle the outer edge of the rotors.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotors are attached to adapter mounts or hubs that are obscured by the angle and overlapping components; no clear lug bolt pattern is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotors show complex internal structures typical of floating or ventilated bicycle disc brakes, with visible gaps between the braking surface and the carrier.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The brake pads are housed inside the caliper body and are not directly visible from this external angle.
Black flexible tubing (hydraulic hoses) is clearly seen entering the caliper bodies.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The braking surfaces of the rotors exhibit a pattern of small, regularly spaced holes (cross-drilled).

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotors appear clean and silver/metallic without significant blueing or browning indicative of heavy heat cycling.
